topics.title: Giving an Account of Visits to Place of Interest: Local Market, Supermarket, Idanre Hill 4 (Basic 4) Second Term 3 and Third Term Week 3 English Studies
topics.content:
GIVING AN ACCOUNT OF VISITS TO PLACE OF INTEREST: LOCAL MARKET, SUPERMARKET, IDANRE HILL PRIMARY 4 (BASIC 4) SECOND TERM WEEK 3 AND THIRD TERM WEEK 3 ENGLISH STUDIES
ENGLISH STUDIES
SECOND TERM WEEK 3
THIRD TERM WEEK 3
PRIMARY 4 (BASIC 4)
THEME - WRITING
TOPIC - PLACES OF INTEREST I
LEARNING AREA
1. Introduction
2. Examples of Places of Interest
3. Summary and Lesson Evaluation
4. Practice Exercise/Assignment/Test Questions and Answers
LEARNING OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, pupils should be able to:
1. explain what a place of interest is.
2. describe a visit to a local market, supermarket, or Idanre Hill.
3. mention activities that take place in these places.
4. give an oral account of a visit to a place of interest.
5. write a short composition about a visit to a place of interest.
ENTRY BEHAVIOUR
The pupils already know how to describe places and events. In this lesson, they will use that knowledge to give an account of visits to places of interest.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of:
1. Pictures of a local market, supermarket, and Idanre Hill
2. Charts showing places of interest
3. Flashcards containing relevant vocabulary
4. Pupils’ notebooks and writing materials
METHOD OF TEACHING
Choose a suitable and appropriate methods for the lessons.
Note - Irrespective of choosing methods of teaching, always introduce an activities that will arouse pupil’s interest or lead them to the lessons.
REFERENCE MATERIALS
1. Scheme of Work
2. 9 - Years Basic Education Curriculum
3. Course Book
4. All Relevant Material
5. Online Information
CONTENT OF THE LESSON
INTRODUCTION
A place of interest is a location that people visit because it is important, useful, beautiful, educational, or exciting. Examples include markets, supermarkets, museums, tourist centres, parks, and hills.
When giving an account of a visit, we explain where we went, what we saw, what happened there, and what we learned from the visit.
1. Local Market
A local market is a place where people buy and sell goods such as food items, clothes, vegetables, and household materials.
Things found in a local market:
- Traders
- Buyers
- Food items
- Fruits and vegetables
- Stalls and shops
2. Supermarket
A supermarket is a large self-service shop where people buy goods arranged on shelves.
Things found in a supermarket:
- Shelves
- Trolleys
- Packaged goods
- Cashiers
- Customers
3. Idanre Hill
Idanre Hill is a famous tourist attraction in Idanre Hill. It is known for its beautiful scenery, ancient settlement, and long stairway leading up the hill.
Things found at Idanre Hill:
- Rocky hills
- Long steps
- Beautiful scenery
- Ancient buildings
- Tourists and guides
SAMPLES: GIVING AN ACCOUNT OF PLACES OF INTEREST
1. A VISIT TO THE LOCAL MARKET
Last Saturday, I visited the local market with my mother. The market was very busy and crowded. Many traders were selling different goods such as food items, fruits, vegetables, clothes, and household materials.
I saw buyers moving from one shop to another to buy what they needed. My mother bought rice, tomatoes, fish, and vegetables. The traders were friendly and attended to customers politely.
The market was noisy because many people were talking, buying, and selling. I enjoyed the visit because I saw many things and learned how people trade in the market.
The visit taught me that the local market is an important place where people buy and sell goods for their daily needs.
2. A VISIT TO THE SUPERMARKET
Last weekend, I visited a supermarket with my father. The supermarket was large, clean, and well arranged. Different goods were neatly displayed on shelves.
I saw food items, drinks, toiletries, books, toys, and many other products. Customers pushed shopping trolleys around the supermarket while selecting the items they wanted to buy.
My father bought rice, milk, biscuits, soap, and fruit juice. After shopping, we went to the cashier to pay for the items. The cashier was polite and friendly.
I enjoyed the visit because the supermarket was neat and organized. The visit taught me how goods are displayed and sold in a modern shopping centre.
A VISIT TO IDANRE HILL
Last holiday, I visited Idanre Hill with my parents. It is one of the most famous tourist attractions in Nigeria.
When we arrived, I saw the beautiful rocky hills and the long staircase leading to the top. The environment was clean and attractive. As we climbed the steps, we enjoyed the fresh air and beautiful scenery around us.
At the top of the hill, I saw ancient buildings, old shrines, and other historical sites. Our guide told us about the history of the people who once lived there. I learned many interesting facts about the culture and traditions of the area.
The visit was exciting and educational. I enjoyed the beautiful view from the hill and took some photographs. It was a memorable experience, and I would love to visit the place again.
PRACTICE EXERCISE/ASSIGNMENT/TEST QUESTIONS AND ANSWERS
A. Fill in the Blanks - Choose the correct words from the box below: supermarket, tourists, traders, shelves, hill, market, customers, goods
1. A local ______ is a place where people buy and sell goods.
2. People who sell items in the market are called ______.
3. Goods in a ______ are neatly arranged on shelves.
4. People who buy things are called ______.
5. Many ______ visit Idanre Hill every year.
6. Idanre Hill is a famous ______ in Ondo State.
7. A supermarket has many ______ for displaying items.
8. People buy and sell ______ in the market.
B. True or False
9. A local market is a place where people buy and sell goods. (______)
10. Goods in a supermarket are usually arranged on shelves. (______)
11. Idanre Hill is located in Lagos State. (______)
12. Tourists visit places of interest. (______)
13. A supermarket is usually clean and well arranged. (______).
C. Match the Places with Their Features
Place - Feature
14. Local Market - a. Long staircase
15. Supermarket - b. Traders and stalls
16. Idanre Hill - c. Shelves and trolleys
D. Composition Writing
17. Write a short account on one of the following:
- A Visit to a Local Market
- A Visit to a Supermarket
- A Visit to Idanre Hill
Your composition should include:
- Where you visited?
- What you saw there?
- Activities that took place.
- What you learned from the visit?
ANSWERS
1. market
2. traders
3. supermarket
4. customers
5. tourists
6. hill
7. shelves
8. goods
9. True
10. True
11. False
12. True
13. True
14. Local Market → b. Traders and stalls
15. Supermarket → c. Shelves and trolleys
16. Idanre Hill → a. Long staircase
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
1. The teacher introduces the lesson by asking pupils about places they have visited.
Pupils’ Activities: The pupils mention places they have visited and share their experiences.
2. The teacher explains the meaning of a place of interest and gives examples such as a local market, supermarket, and Idanre Hill.
Pupils’ Activities: The pupils listen attentively and ask questions.
3. The teacher displays pictures of a local market, supermarket, and Idanre Hill and discusses their features.
Pupils’ Activities: The pupils identify and describe what they see in the pictures.
4. The teacher explains the activities that take place in each location.
Pupils’ Activities: The pupils mention activities that occur in the places.
5. The teacher reads a sample account of a visit to a local market.
Pupils’ Activities: The pupils listen and identify important details in the account.
6. The teacher reads a sample account of a visit to a supermarket and Idanre Hill.
Pupils’ Activities: The pupils compare the different experiences described.
7. The teacher guides pupils to give oral accounts of places they have visited using simple sentences.
Pupils’ Activities: The pupils narrate their experiences before the class.
8. The teacher guides pupils to write short accounts of visits to places of interest in their notebooks.
Pupils’ Activities: The pupils write their accounts using correct sentences.
9. The teacher marks pupils’ work, corrects errors, and summarizes the lesson.
Pupils’ Activities: The pupils make corrections and participate in the lesson summary.
CONCLUSION
To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.
LESSON EVALUATION
Teacher asks pupils,
1. what is a place of interest?
2. mention three examples of places of interest.
3. what can people buy in a local market?
4. who attends to customers in a supermarket?
5. in which state is Idanre Hill located?
ANSWERS
1. A place people visit because it is useful, interesting, educational, or beautiful.
2. Local market, supermarket, Idanre Hill.
3. Food items, fruits, vegetables, clothes, and household materials.
4. Cashiers or sales attendants.
5. Ondo State.

topics.title: Giving an Account of Visits to Place of Interest: Tourist Attraction, Hospital and Court of Law 4 (Basic 4) Second Term 3 Week 4 and Third Term Week 4 English Studies
topics.content:
GIVING AN ACCOUNT OF VISITS TO PLACE OF INTEREST: TOURIST ATTRACTION, HOSPITAL AND COURT OF LAW SECOND TERM WEEK 4 AND THIRD TERM WEEK 4 ENGLISH STUDIES
ENGLISH STUDIES
SECOND TERM WEEK 4
THIRD TERM WEEK 4
PRIMARY 4 (BASIC 4)
THEME - STRUCTURE
TOPIC - PLACE OF INTEREST II
LEARNING AREA
1. Introduction
2. Examples of Places of Interest
3. Summary and Lesson Evaluation
4. Practice Exercise/Assignment/Test Questions and Answers
LEARNING OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, pupils should be able to:
1. explain the meaning of a place of interest.
2. describe a visit to a tourist attraction, hospital, and court of law.
3. mention important features of each place.
4. give an oral account of a visit to any of the places.
5. write a short composition on a visit to a place of interest.
ENTRY BEHAVIOUR
The pupils already know how to describe places and events. In this lesson, they will extend that knowledge by giving accounts of visits to a tourist attraction, hospital, and court of law.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of:
1. Pictures of a tourist attraction, hospital, and court of law
Charts showing activities in each place
Flashcards containing relevant vocabulary
Pupils’ notebooks and writing materials
METHOD OF TEACHING
Choose a suitable and appropriate methods for the lessons.
Note - Irrespective of choosing methods of teaching, always introduce an activities that will arouse pupil’s interest or lead them to the lessons.
REFERENCE MATERIALS
1. Scheme of Work
2. 9 - Years Basic Education Curriculum
3. Course Book
4. All Relevant Material
5. Online Information
CONTENT OF THE LESSON
INTRODUCTION
A place of interest is a place people visit because it is important, educational, useful, or attractive. Examples include tourist attractions, hospitals, courts of law, museums, parks, and markets.
When giving an account of a visit, we explain where we went, what we saw, what happened there, and what we learned from the visit.
EXAMPLES OF PLACE OF INTEREST
1. Tourist Attraction
A tourist attraction is a place that attracts visitors because of its beauty, history, culture, or special features.
Things Found at a Tourist Attraction
- Tourists
- Tour guides
- Beautiful scenery
- Historical objects
- Recreational facilities
2. Hospital
A hospital is a place where sick or injured people receive medical treatment.
Things Found in a Hospital
- Doctors
- Nurses
- Patients
- Medicines
- Ambulances
3. Court of Law
A court of law is a place where legal matters are heard and justice is administered.
Things Found in a Court of Law
- Judge
- Lawyers
- Witnesses
- Court clerk
- Security officers
SAMPLES: GIVING AN ACCOUNT OF VISITS TO PLACE OF INTEREST
1. A VISIT TO A TOURIST ATTRACTION
Last holiday, I visited a tourist attraction with my parents. The place was beautiful and very interesting. Many people came from different places to see the attraction.
When we arrived, I saw beautiful scenery, trees, and historical objects. There were many tourists taking photographs and enjoying the environment. A tour guide showed us around and explained the history of the place.
I learned many new things about the culture and history of the area. The visit was both educational and entertaining. I enjoyed every moment of the trip.
It was a wonderful experience, and I would like to visit the tourist attraction again in the future.
2. A VISIT TO A HOSPITAL
Last month, I visited a hospital with my mother to see my uncle, who was receiving treatment. The hospital was neat, quiet, and well organized.
When we arrived, I saw doctors and nurses attending to patients. Some patients were waiting to see the doctor, while others were receiving treatment. The nurses were kind and caring to the patients.
I also saw an ambulance parked outside the hospital. The doctors examined patients and prescribed medicines to help them recover from their illnesses.
The visit taught me that hospitals are important places where sick and injured people receive care and treatment. I enjoyed the visit and learned the importance of good health and hygiene.
3. A VISIT TO A COURT OF LAW
Last term, my classmates and I visited a court of law with our teacher. The visit was educational and interesting.
When we arrived, we saw a large courtroom. The judge was seated at the front of the court, while the lawyers stood to present their cases. We also saw witnesses giving evidence and court officials carrying out their duties.
The courtroom was quiet and orderly. Everyone listened carefully as the judge heard the cases and made decisions based on the law.
During the visit, we learned that a court of law is a place where justice is administered and disputes are settled peacefully. The visit taught me the importance of obeying the law, telling the truth, and respecting the rights of others.
I enjoyed the visit and learned many valuable lessons about justice and good citizenship.
PRACTICE EXERCISE/HOMEWORK/TEST QUESTIONS AND ANSWERS
A. Fill in the Blanks - Choose from the box: judge, doctor, tourist, nurse, lawyer, patient, attraction, justice
1. A _______ treats sick people.
2. A _______ assists the doctor.
3. A person who visits a tourist site is a _______.
4. A _______ presides over a court.
5. A _______ represents people in court.
6. A sick person in a hospital is called a _______.
7. A tourist site is a tourist _______.
8. Courts help to maintain _______.
ANSWERS
1. doctor
2. nurse
3. tourist
4. judge
5. lawyer
6. patient
7. attraction
8. justice
SUMMARY
Pupils learned how to give an account of visits to places of interest such as a tourist attraction, hospital, and court of law, and identified the important activities and people found in each place.
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
1. The teacher introduces the lesson by asking pupils to mention places they have visited outside their homes and schools.
Pupils’ Activities: The pupils mention places they have visited and share their experiences.
2. The teacher explains the meaning of a place of interest and gives examples such as tourist attractions, hospitals, and courts of law.
Pupils’ Activities: The pupils listen attentively and ask questions.
3. The teacher displays pictures of a tourist attraction, hospital, and court of law.
Pupils’ Activities: The pupils observe the pictures and identify what they see.
4. The teacher explains the features and activities found in a tourist attraction.
Pupils’ Activities: The pupils mention things they know about tourist attractions.
5. The teacher explains the features and activities found in a hospital.
Pupils’ Activities: The pupils identify people and items commonly found in a hospital.
6. The teacher explains the features and activities found in a court of law.
Pupils’ Activities: The pupils identify the people who work in a court and their duties.
7. The teacher reads sample accounts of visits to the three places and discusses them with the class.
Pupils’ Activities: The pupils listen carefully and answer questions based on the accounts.
8. The teacher guides pupils to give oral accounts of visits they have made to any place of interest.
Pupils’ Activities: The pupils narrate their experiences using simple sentences.
9. The teacher guides pupils to write short accounts of visits to a tourist attraction, hospital, or court of law.
Pupils’ Activities: The pupils write their compositions in their notebooks.
10. The teacher marks pupils’ work, corrects errors, and summarizes the lesson.
Pupils’ Activities: The pupils make corrections and participate in the lesson summary.
CONCLUSION
To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.
LESSON EVALUATION
Teacher asks pupils,
1. what is a place of interest?
2. mention three examples of places of interest.
3. who works in a hospital?
4. who presides over a court of law?
5. what is the importance of a tourist attraction?
ANSWERS
1. A place people visit because it is useful, educational, or interesting.
2. Tourist attraction, hospital, court of law.
3. Doctors and nurses.
4. A judge.
5. It provides education, recreation, and sightseeing.

topics.title: Aural Discrimination: Vowel Sounds /ʌ/ and /ɜ:/ Primary 4 (Basic 4) Second/Third Term Week 5 English Studies
topics.content:
AURAL DISCRIMINATION: SOUNDS /ʌ/ and /ɜ:/ SECOND/THIRD TERM WEEK 5 ENGLISH STUDIES
ENGLISH STUDIES
SECOND/THIRD TERM
WEEK 5
PRIMARY 4 (BASIC 4)
THEME - SPEECH WORK
TOPIC - SOUNDS /ʌ/ and /ɜ:/
LEARNING AREA
1. Introduction
2. Miminal Pairs
3. Pronunciation Practice/Oral Drills
4. Summary and Lesson Evaluation
5. Practice Exercise/Homework/Test Questions and Answers
LEARNING OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, pupils should be able to:
1. identify the vowel sounds /ʌ/ and /ɜː/.
2. pronounce words containing the sounds correctly.
3. distinguish between words containing /ʌ/ and /ɜː/.
4. listen carefully and identify the sounds in spoken words.
5. use words containing the sounds in simple sentences.
ENTRY BEHAVIOUR
The pupils can already identify and pronounce some vowel sounds. This lesson will help them distinguish between the vowel sounds /ʌ/ and /ɜː/.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of:
1. Flashcards containing words with /ʌ/ and /ɜː/.
2. Pronunciation charts.
3. Whiteboard and marker/chalkboard and chalk.
4. English Language textbook.
5. Audio recordings (if available).
6. Pupils’ notebooks and writing materials.
METHOD OF TEACHING
Choose a suitable and appropriate methods for the lessons.
Note - Irrespective of choosing methods of teaching, always introduce an activities that will arouse pupil’s interest or lead them to the lessons.
REFERENCE MATERIALS
1. Scheme of Work
2. 9 - Years Basic Education Curriculum
3. Course Book
4. All Relevant Material
5. Online Information
CONTENT OF THE LESSON
INTRODUCTION
Aural discrimination is the ability to listen carefully and distinguish between different speech sounds. It helps pupils develop good pronunciation, listening, speaking, reading, and spelling skills.
In English, some vowel sounds may sound similar, but they are pronounced differently. In this lesson, pupils will learn to identify and distinguish between the vowel sounds /ʌ/ and /ɜː/.
Examples of Sound /ʌ/
- cup
- sun
- bus
- run
- hut
Examples of Sound /ɜː/
- bird
- girl
- nurse
- shirt
- church
MINIMAL PAIRS
Sounds /ʌ/ - /ɜː/
- bun - burn
- cut - curt
- luck - lurk
- bus - burst
- hut - hurt
PRONUNCIATION PRACTICE/ORAL DRILLS
Repeat After the Teacher
1. Sound /ʌ/
- cup
- sun
- bus
- run
- hut
2. Sound /ɜː/
- bird
- girl
- nurse
- shirt
- church
3. Minimal Pairs
- bun - burn
- cut - curt
- luck - lurk
- hut - hurt
- bus - burst
SUMMARY
Pupils learned how to identify, pronounce, and distinguish between the vowel sounds /ʌ/ and /ɜː/ through listening activities, pronunciation drills, and practice exercises.
PRACTICE EXERCISE/ASSIGNMENT/TEST QUESTIONS AND ANSWERS
A. Circle the Word with the /ʌ/ Sound
1. cup - bird
2. sun - girl
3. bus - nurse
4. run - shirt
5. hut - church
B. Circle the Word with the /ɜː/ Sound
6. cup - bird
7. sun - girl
8. bus - nurse
9. run - shirt
10. hut - church
C. Pronounce the Following Words
11. cup
12. sun
13. bird
14. nurse
15. shirt
ANSWERS
1. cup
2. sun
3. bus
4. run
5. hut
6. bird
7. girl
8. nurse
9. shirt
10. church
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
1. The teacher introduces the vowel sounds /ʌ/ and /ɜː/ and pronounces them clearly.
Pupils’ Activities: The pupils listen carefully and repeat the sounds after the teacher.
2. The teacher presents words containing the /ʌ/ sound.
Examples:
- cup
- sun
- bus
- run
- hut
Pupils’ Activities: The pupils repeat the words and identify the /ʌ/ sound.
3. The teacher presents words containing the /ɜː/ sound.
Examples:
- bird
- girl
- nurse
- shirt
- church
Pupils’ Activities: The pupils repeat the words and identify the /ɜː/ sound.
4. The teacher writes pairs of words on the board and pronounces them.
Examples:
- bun - burn
- cut - curt
- luck - lurk
- hut - hurt
- bus - burst
Pupils’ Activities: The pupils listen carefully and identify the differences in pronunciation.
5. The teacher drills the pupils on the correct pronunciation of the minimal pairs.
Pupils’ Activities: The pupils repeat the words individually and in groups.
6. The teacher pronounces words randomly and asks pupils to identify whether they contain the /ʌ/ or /ɜː/ sound.
Pupils’ Activities: The pupils listen and identify the correct sound.
7. The teacher guides pupils to use some of the words in simple sentences.
Pupils’ Activities: The pupils make oral and written sentences using the words.
8. The teacher corrects pupils’ pronunciation and provides further practice where necessary.
Pupils’ Activities: The pupils repeat the words correctly and make corrections.
9. The teacher summarizes the lesson by revising the sounds /ʌ/ and /ɜː/ and their examples.
Pupils’ Activities: The pupils participate in the lesson summary and answer oral questions.
CONCLUSION
To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.
LESSON EVALUATION
Teacher asks pupils,
1. mention two words with the /ʌ/ sound.
2. mention two words with the /ɜː/ sound.
3. pronounce: cup and bird.
4. pronounce: hut and hurt.
5. state the difference between the sounds /ʌ/ and /ɜː/.

topics.title: Possessive Determiners Primary 4 (Basic 4) Third Term Week 10 English Studies
topics.content:
POSSESSIVE DETERMINERS PRIMARY 4 (BASIC 4) THIRD TERM WEEK 10 ENGLISH STUDIES
ENGLISH STUDIES
SECOND TERM
WEEK 10
PRIMARY 4 (BASIC 4)
THEME - WRITING
TOPIC - POSSESSIVE DETERMINERS
LEARNING AREA
1. Introduction
2. Examples of Possessive Determiners
3. Making Sentences with Possessive Determiners
4. Summary and Lesson Evaluation
5. Practice Exercise/Homework/Test Questions and Answers
LEARNING OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, pupils should be able to:
1. define possessive determiners.
2. identify possessive determiners in sentences.
3. mention examples of possessive determiners.
4. use possessive determiners correctly in sentences.
5. construct simple sentences using possessive determiners.
ENTRY BEHAVIOUR
The pupils already know that determiners are words placed before nouns. This lesson introduces possessive determiners, which show ownership or possession.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of:
1. Flashcards containing possessive determiners.
2. Charts showing examples of possessive determiners.
3. Whiteboard and marker/chalkboard and chalk.
4. English Language textbook.
5. Real objects in the classroom.
6. Pupils’ notebooks and writing materials.
METHOD OF TEACHING
Choose a suitable and appropriate methods for the lessons.
Note - Irrespective of choosing methods of teaching, always introduce an activities that will arouse pupil’s interest or lead them to the lessons.
REFERENCE MATERIALS
1. Scheme of Work
2. 9 - Years Basic Education Curriculum
3. Course Book
4. All Relevant Material
5. Online Information
CONTENT OF THE LESSON
INTRODUCTION
Possessive determiners are words used before nouns to show ownership or possession. They tell us who owns or has a particular person, animal, place, or thing.
They always come before nouns and tell us who owns or possesses something.
Examples of Possessive Determiners
- my
- your
- his
- her
- its
- our
- their
Examples in Sentences
- This is my book.
- Is that your bag?
- His shirt is blue.
- Her pencil is sharp.
- The dog is wagging its tail.
- Our classroom is clean.
- Their teacher is kind.
SUMMARY
Pupils learned that possessive determiners are words used before nouns to show ownership or possession. They also identified and used my, your, his, her, its, our, and their correctly in sentences.
PRACTICE EXERCISE/ASSIGNMENT/TEST QUESTIONS AND ANSWERS
A. Fill in the Blanks with the Correct Possessive Determiner
1. This is ____ book.
2. That is ____ bag.
3. ____ shirt is clean.
4. ____ pencil is sharp.
5. ____ classroom is neat.
B. Underline the Possessive Determiner
6. My pencil is on the table.
7. Her dress is beautiful.
8. Their teacher is friendly.
9. Our school is large.
10. His book is interesting.
C. Construct Sentences Using:
11. my
12. your
13. our
14. their
ANSWERS
1. my
2. your
3. his
4. her
5. our
6. My
7. Her
8. Their
9. Our
10. His
11. My bag is new.
12. Your book is on the desk.
13. Our classroom is clean.
14. Their house is beautiful.
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
1. The teacher revises the meaning of determiners and asks pupils to mention some examples.
Pupils’ Activities: The pupils respond and give examples of determiners.
2. The teacher introduces possessive determiners and explains that they show ownership or possession.
Pupils’ Activities: The pupils listen attentively and participate in the discussion.
3. The teacher writes the possessive determiners on the board:
- my
- your
- his
- her
- its
- our
- their
Pupils’ Activities: The pupils read the words aloud.
4. The teacher explains the use of each possessive determiner with examples.
Examples:
- My book is on the table.
- Your bag is new.
- His shirt is clean.
- Her pencil is sharp.
- Our classroom is neat.
- Their teacher is kind.
Pupils’ Activities: The pupils identify the possessive determiners in the sentences.
5. The teacher uses classroom objects to demonstrate ownership.
Examples:
- This is my marker.
- That is your notebook.
Pupils’ Activities: The pupils identify the owners of the objects.
6. The teacher writes sentences on the board and asks pupils to fill in suitable possessive determiners.
Pupils’ Activities: The pupils complete the sentences correctly.
7. The teacher guides pupils to construct oral and written sentences using possessive determiners.
Pupils’ Activities: The pupils make sentences individually and in groups.
8. The teacher gives class exercises and corrects pupils’ mistakes.
Pupils’ Activities: The pupils complete the exercises and make corrections.
9. The teacher summarizes the lesson by revising the meaning and uses of possessive determiners.
Pupils’ Activities: The pupils answer oral questions and participate in the lesson summary.
CONCLUSION
To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.
LESSON EVALUATION
Teacher asks pupils,
1. what are possessive determiners?
2. mention four possessive determiners.
3. use my in a sentence.
4. use their in a sentence.
5. what does a possessive determiner show?

topics.title: Article Determiners Primary 4 (Basic 4) Second/Third Term Week 10 English Studies
topics.content:
ARTICLE DETERMINERS PRIMARY 4 (BASIC 4) SECOND/THIRD TERM WEEK 10 ENGLISH STUDIES
ENGLISH STUDIES
SECOND/THIRD TERM
WEEK 10
PRIMARY 4 (BASIC 4)
THEME - SPEECH WORK
TOPIC - ARTICLE DETERMINERS
LEARNING AREA
1. Introduction
2. Uses of Article Determiners
3. Making Sentences Using Article Determiners
4. Practice Exercise/Test Questions and Answers
5. Summary
LEARNING OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, pupils should be able to:
1. define article determiners.
2. identify article determiners in sentences.
3. mention the three article determiners.
4. use a, an, and the correctly in sentences.
4. construct simple sentences using article determiners.
ENTRY BEHAVIOUR
The pupils already know that determiners are words placed before nouns. This lesson introduces article determiners, which help to identify specific or non-specific nouns.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of:
1. Flashcards showing a, an, and the.
2. Charts containing examples of article determiners.
3. Whiteboard and marker/chalkboard and chalk.
4. English Language textbook.
5. Real objects in the classroom.
6. Pupils’ notebooks and writing materials.
METHOD OF TEACHING
Choose a suitable and appropriate methods for the lessons.
Note - Irrespective of choosing methods of teaching, always introduce an activities that will arouse pupil’s interest or lead them to the lessons.
REFERENCE MATERIALS
1. Scheme of Work
2. 9 - Years Basic Education Curriculum
3. Course Book
4. All Relevant Material
5. Online Information
CONTENT OF THE LESSON
INTRODUCTION
Determiners are words placed before nouns to give more information about them. One type of determiner is the article determiner.
Article determiners are words placed before nouns to show whether the noun is general or specific. That’s, they help us know whether we are talking about a particular person, animal, place, or thing, or about one in general.
The article determiners are:
- a
- an
- the
USES OF ARTICLE DETERMINERS
A
A is used before singular nouns that begin with a consonant sound.
Examples:
- a boy
- a pen
- a book
Sentences:
- I have a pencil.
- She saw a dog.
- A boy is playing football.
An
An is used before singular nouns that begin with a vowel sound.
Examples:
- an egg
- an orange
- an umbrella
Sentences:
- I ate an apple.
- She bought an orange.
- An orange is on the table.
The
The is used before specific nouns already known to the speaker and listener.
Examples:
- the teacher
- the classroom
- the market
Sentences:
- The teacher is teaching.
- The book is on the table.
- The teacher is in the classroom.
EXAMPLES IN SENTENCES
- A boy is playing football.
- An elephant is a large animal.
- The pupils are in the classroom.
- I saw a bird in the tree.
- She ate an egg for breakfast.
SUMMARY
Article determiners help us speak and write correctly by showing whether a noun is general or specific. Pupils learned that article determiners are words used before nouns. They identified and used a, an, and the correctly in sentences.
PRACTICE EXERCISE/HOMEWORK/TEST QUESTIONS AND ANSWERS
A. Fill in the Blanks with a, an, or the
1. I saw ____ elephant at the zoo.
2. She has ____ pen.
3. ____ teacher is in the classroom.
4. He ate ____ orange.
5. We visited ____ market yesterday.
B. Underline the Article Determiner
6. A boy is running.
7. An umbrella is on the table.
8. The pupils are singing.
9. I saw a bird.
10. The book belongs to me.
C. Construct sentences using the following words in sentences:
11. a
12. an
13. the
ANSWERS
1. an
2. a
3. The
4. an
5. the
6. A
7. An
8. The
9. a
10. The
11. A girl is dancing.
12. An apple is on the table.
13. The teacher is teaching.
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
1. The teacher revises the meaning of determiners and asks pupils to mention some examples.
Pupils’ Activities: The pupils respond and give examples of determiners.
2. The teacher introduces article determiners and writes a, an, and the on the board.
Pupils’ Activities: The pupils read the words aloud.
3. The teacher explains the use of a before singular nouns beginning with consonant sounds.
Examples:
- a boy
- a book
- a pen
Pupils’ Activities: The pupils identify more examples and use them in sentences.
4. The teacher explains the use of an before singular nouns beginning with vowel sounds.
Examples:
- an egg
- an orange
- an umbrella
Pupils’ Activities: The pupils identify more examples and use them in sentences.
5. The teacher explains the use of the before specific nouns.
Examples:
- the teacher
- the classroom
- the market
Pupils’ Activities: The pupils listen and provide additional examples.
6. The teacher writes sentences on the board and asks pupils to identify the article determiners.
Examples:
- A girl is singing.
- An apple is on the table.
- The pupils are in the classroom.
Pupils’ Activities: The pupils identify and underline the article determiners.
7. The teacher guides pupils to complete sentences using a, an, and the correctly.
Pupils’ Activities: The pupils complete the sentences orally and in writing.
8. The teacher asks pupils to construct their own sentences using the three article determiners.
Pupils’ Activities: The pupils make oral and written sentences.
9. The teacher corrects pupils’ mistakes and summarizes the lesson.
Pupils’ Activities: The pupils make corrections and participate in the lesson summary.
CONCLUSION
To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.
LESSON EVALUATION
Teacher asks pupils,
1. what are article determiners?
2. mention the three article determiners.
3. use a in a sentence.
4. use an in a sentence.
5. state one difference between a and an.
